name: Nullvault Cleanroom Iso-Suit Type-C
description:
Crisp white single-piece coverall with sealed hood, integrated booties, and triple-layer glove cuffs. Shell is electrostatically dissipative polyethylene composite — stiff, crinkles audibly when moved, and carries a faint antiseptic smell that never fully washes out. Designed for Class-10 cleanroom chip fabrication environments and geneware clinic sterile theaters.

Face shield is optically clear with anti-static coating. All seams are ultrasonically welded, no stitching. A narrow laminated panel on the left forearm accepts a BCI proximity ID card. Geneware workers with tails or wings cannot use standard Type-C — they require the gene-compatible Type-G variant at three times the cost.
functionality: Rated ISO Class 5 particulate exclusion. ESD dissipation prevents static discharge near sensitive fab equipment. Integrated BCI ID panel logs entry/exit times automatically. Positive-pressure hood option available on Type-C Plus variant. Single-use or up to 12 sterilization cycles before mandatory disposal.
what_it_says: You work somewhere clean enough that your body is considered a contamination risk.
manufacturer: Nullvault Sterile Systems (Corponation subsidiary of Helix Corp)
price_range: Φ 45–Φ 120 per unit (bulk facility purchase Φ 28/unit)
story_hooks: A geneware clinic has been cutting costs by reusing single-use Type-C suits past the 12-cycle limit — and a contamination outbreak is being quietly suppressed.
A chip fab worker has been smuggling data out encoded in the BCI ID log metadata — no one has noticed because the logs are auto-archived and never reviewed.
A Type-C suit was found abandoned in a Tier 1 drainage channel, still sealed, with biological material inside that doesn't match any known geneware profile.
